Review the README.md and /src files for details about the repository purpose and structure and update this overview accordingly.

.NET 10.0 (`net10.0`), latest C#, nullable/implicit usings enabled, `TreatWarningsAsErrors=true`; Warning 1591 suppressed via `NoWarn`. All projects inherit [Directory.Build.props](Directory.Build.props); use its analyzers and consider NSDepCop. Structure: `src/`, `tests/`, `Directory.Build.props`, `Directory.Packages.props`, `Template.slnx`.

Uses MSBuild Central Package Management (`ManagePackageVersionsCentrally=true`). Versions are managed in [Directory.Packages.props](Directory.Packages.props); projects omit package versions. Add packages with `<PackageVersion Include="PackageName" Version="x.y.z" />`.

Use file-scoped namespaces outside namespace: `namespace MyProject.Feature;`; `_myField`, PascalCase constants, `var` for built-in/apparent types, `I` interfaces, `Async` methods. Use 2 spaces, CRLF, UTF-8 BOM, Allman braces, and braces except single-line exits. Primary constructors preferred; ALWAYS assign to readonly fields. Prefer top-level entry points, pattern matching, and expression-bodied properties/indexers/accessors (not methods). Run `dotnet format`.

Use `appsettings.json`, `appsettings.{Environment}.json`, `IConfiguration`, `IOptions<T>`, strongly typed settings, and User Secrets. Never hardcode sensitive information in source code. Use `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging`, suitable levels, context, structured logging, correlation IDs where possible, and avoid sensitive data.

Use `Ardalis.GuardClauses` for non-UI validation and prefer `FluentValidation` for complex/UI validation. UI invalid input must produce user-friendly error messages; non-UI invalid input must throw appropriate exceptions using guard clauses. Return suitable HTTP status codes. Follow OWASP: validate/sanitize inputs, parameterized queries/ORM, authentication/authorization, HTTPS.

Write unit testable code. Offer to add tests to generated code if applicable - place such tests in the `tests/` folder. Only test code that you control and that has business logic; do not test framework code. Use focused classes, Dependency Injection, composition, async/await for I/O, methods ideally under 20 lines, parameter objects above 4 arguments. Prefer FastEndpoints `REPR`, DDD, DTOs, and `*Request`/`*Response`, `*Command`/`*Query`, `*Details`/`*Summary`. Avoid locating interfaces and implementations in the same project.

Production projects go in `src/`, test projects in `tests/`; test projects should use `xUnit`.

dotnet run --project src/YourProject/YourProject.csproj

Use `xUnit`; Arrange-Act-Assert with whitespace separation, no comments. Organize feature folders mirroring `src/`. Do not name test classes with "Tests" suffix; do use "Tests" suffix for folder names if needed. Use `[Fact]`, `[Theory]`, `[InlineData]`; NSubstitute; Shouldly. Name classes `ClassName_MethodName.cs`, methods `DoesSomething_GivenSomeCondition`, forming a sentence. Example: `ProductServiceTests/ProductService_Constructor.cs`; `ProductService_Constructor._ReturnsInstanceGivenValidInputs`. Separate unit/integration tests. Avoid commercially licensed testing libraries (e.g. FluentAssertions, Moq).

Use Markdown documentation, headings, syntax-highlighted snippets, blank lines around lists/code listings, and run linting tools. See [.editorconfig](.editorconfig), [Directory.Build.props](Directory.Build.props), [Directory.Packages.props](Directory.Packages.props), and [.gitignore](.gitignore).
